newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Adsteam plans maritime unit float.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Adsteam plans maritime unit float.

text.p: The Adelaide Steamship Co Ltd said on Friday that it proposed to float its maritime operations.

Adsteam chairman Peter Cottrell said the proposal would be outlined in an explanatory memorandum to be sent to shareholders early next week. The proposal allows for a float of the 122 year-old operations at any time before March 31 next year.

Cottrell said the terms of the float would provide shareholders with a two cent per share payment, the ability to participate in a priority allocation of up to 20 percent of the shares to be issued, and retention of their existing interest in the other assets and liabilities.
Shareholders would also be asked to change Adsteam's name to Residual Assco Group Ltd.
The name change would allow the maritime assets to operate under the name "Adsteam Marine" if the float proceeded.
Cottrell said funds raised would be used to further reduce debt.
Adsteam was one of Australia's largest corporate failure following the debt binge of the 1980s.

It came under the control of its bank creditors in 1990 with debts of A$11 billion, which has now been reduced to less than A$700 million. Woolworths Ltd and David Jones Ltd were once part of the Adsteam group and were floated by the creditors.
Shareholders would vote on the float and the proposed name changes at a general meeting in Adelaide on April 9.
The maritime unit consisted of an extensive harbour towage and marine services operation in more than 33 Australian ports and another four ports in Papua New Guinea and Fiji.

Adsteam said the unit was Australia's largest marine towage operator with a fleet of 45 vessels, including some owned in joint ventures with Howard Smith Ltd and the Stannard family. The unit's 1995/96 pre-tax operating profit rose by A$4 million to A$19.6 million.
